reasons: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of Customer-specific Deliverables in Vendor and grants only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence back, which fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense) — a genuine deviation, not an acceptable fallback.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it reverses ownership, adds an express present assignment of IP rights in each Deliverable, and expressly carves out Vendor Technology so Vendor's pre-existing platform IP is preserved (consistent with the rule's note that Vendor keeping its platform is fine).

The high changed-character ratio (0.778) is justified here because reversing the assignment direction necessarily rewrites the sentence; the edit stays confined to p0054 and does not disturb Sections 14.1, 14.3 or 14.4, which the rationale correctly identifies as already satisfactory (no double-flagging of Customer Data ownership or joint ownership).

The comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, and correctly notes that the Section 13.2 perpetual licence only covers Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable and therefore does not cure the revocable term-limited licence.
